summary: Sabah Airport (SBV) is a small domestic airfield serving the community of Sabah on Bougainville Island in the Autonomous Region of Bougainville, Papua New Guinea. The airport provides essential air access to this remote part of the South Pacific, supporting local travel, cargo transport, and connections to Buka and other regional centers. Its modest infrastructure reflects the rugged, tropical setting of northern Bougainville, where aviation remains a vital link to the outside world.
faqs:
Q: What is the airport code for Sabah Airport?
A: The IATA code is SBV and the ICAO code is AYSH.

Q: Are there regular commercial flights to Sabah Airport?
A: Service is limited to occasional domestic flights operated by small aircraft, typical of remote Papua New Guinea airfields. Schedules may vary based on demand and weather conditions.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a small regional airport, facilities are basic, generally limited to a small terminal area and minimal passenger services.

Q: Which airlines serve Sabah Airport?
A: Small regional carriers operating in the Bougainville region provide intermittent scheduled or charter service to the airport.
transport_tips: Ground transportation options at Sabah Airport are limited, so arranging a local vehicle in advance is highly recommended. Road access can be challenging, particularly after heavy rainfall, so allow extra travel time when driving to or from the airfield. Many travelers rely on local contacts or accommodations to coordinate pickup and drop-off.
local_tip: Pack light and bring waterproof bags—humidity and unexpected tropical showers are common, and baggage handling at small Papua New Guinea airfields can be rough on luggage.
